text:
Alyssa: Quick Q — I flipped inference-svc from LoadBalancer -> ClusterIP in Terraform and plugged an HTTPRoute to the Gateway API for canary routing. After deploy, prod traffic to /v1/generate is returning a bunch of 502s from the ALB. Anyone seen this pattern after a service type change?

Derek: Did you also change port names on the Service? Gateway/HTTPRoute often needs named ports or exact port numbers to match backend refs.

Alyssa: I only changed type and removed the ephemeral nodePort bits. Service ports are currently unnamed. HTTPRoute backendRef is using port: 8080 (number). Gateway is an AWS ALB with TLS termination.

Kai: Can you paste the service snippet + httproute yaml and the terraform diff? small clues help.

Alyssa: Sure — terraform fragment (before/after):
```hcl
# before
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference" {
  metadata { name = "inference-svc" namespace = "inference-prod" }
  spec {
    type = "LoadBalancer"
    port { port = 80 target_port = 8080 }
  }
}

# after
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference" {
  metadata { name = "inference-svc" namespace = "inference-prod" }
  spec {
    type = "ClusterIP"
    port { port = 80 target_port = 8080 }
  }
}
```
HTTPRoute:
```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: inference-route
  namespace: inference-prod
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: main-gateway
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path:
            type: PathPrefix
            value: /v1/generate
      backendRefs:
        - backendRef:
            name: inference-svc
            port: 8080
```

Alyssa: ALB health shows target group unhealthy, 502s spike. kubectl describe svc shows no port names.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] applied terraform change by @Alyssa in infra/inference (plan -> apply).

Derek: If HTTPRoute backendRef.port is a number it should match, but some implementations prefer named ports (and some service-proxy layer requires port names like "http" or "https" to pick proper protocol). Also double-check the Gateway's listener is forwarding to the right gateway namespace and that the Gateway has the TLSSecret correctly referenced.

Maria: I ran into something similar — our ALB ingress controller will create target groups per port name. If a Service has multiple ports with no names or ambiguous mapping, it can attach the wrong port/target group or create one with node port that isn't open.

Kai: Can you run these quick checks?
- kubectl get svc inference-svc -n inference-prod -o yaml
- kubectl get httproute inference-route -n inference-prod -o yaml
- kubectl describe targetgroup <tg-id> in AWS for the port and healthcheck path

Alyssa: Output excerpt (svc):
```yaml
spec:
  clusterIP: 10.0.42.12
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP
```
httproute shows backendRef port 8080 as above.

Derek: Hmm. Another angle — Gateway TLS secret binding. If ALB is terminating TLS and forwarding HTTP to port 80 on the pod, but the backend healthcheck expects /health on 8080, healthcheck path mismatch could fail with 502. What does target group healthcheck use? Also check externalTrafficPolicy (Local vs Cluster) — with ClusterIP that shouldn't matter, but the ALB controller still maps through nodes.

Alyssa: Target group healthcheck is /health on port 80. Our app listens on 8080 and responds on /health there. So TG is hitting port 80 but service forwards to 8080 — that should be fine. But controller may have registered node port instead (which we removed).

Kai: Proposed quick fixes:
1) Add explicit names to service ports (e.g., name: http) and use backendRef.port.name in the HTTPRoute.
2) Ensure the Gateway TLS secret is in the same namespace as the Gateway resource (ALB controller needs that).
3) Temporarily revert to LoadBalancer if this is blocking production.

Derek: Example patch:
```hcl
spec {
  type = "ClusterIP"
  port { name = "http" port = 80 target_port = 8080 }
}
```
And change HTTPRoute backendRef to: 
```yaml
backendRefs:
  - backendRef:
      name: inference-svc
      port: 
        name: http
```

Maria: Also check that the Pod spec listens on containerPort: 8080 and that readiness probe is healthy. If readiness failing, endpoints empty -> 502.

Alyssa: Good call. I checked endpoints — empty for a while during deploy, but they came back healthy. Readiness probe is /ready on 8080 and was green.

infra-bot: [alert] 502 spike detected on inference-prod at 1987654365.

Alyssa: I pushed the port name change and updated HTTPRoute to reference name. Reapplying now. Will monitor.

Derek: Nice. If that fixes it, we should update the terraform module for all services to include port_name param and add a tfvar to opt-in.

Alyssa: Update — patch rolled, ALB target group now shows healthy, 502s cleared. Thanks all. I'll open a follow-up PR to make port names mandatory in the service module and add a brief note about Gateway/ALB edge cases.

Kai: Thanks for the quick triage. If you want I can help write the PR with a test manifest.

Alyssa: Please do — assign it to me and Derek. :thumbsup:
